- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is negative or volatile (e.g., post-0.29 sentiment bump).
- Underestimate sharp upward moves when sentiment is mildly negative (e.g., -0.10 to -0.30) — model tends to lag or underreact.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., -0.40+), reduce forecasted mean by 0.5–1.5% relative to prior 30d average.
- Avoid over-optimistic 30d forecasts when recent 18d history shows mean reversion (e.g., 78.3–79.5 range with 78.8+ true outcome).
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.07–0.29), model tends to overpredict — cap forecast at 1.5–2.0% above recent 18d high.
- Lagged corrections: if true outcome exceeds forecast by >1.5% in 3–5 days, adjust next forecast downward by 0.5–1.0% to avoid overshoot.
- For 30d horizon, if sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., -0.50+), apply a 0.8–1.2% downward bias to avoid overconfidence in recovery.
